name: Cutting cycle

card.summary: A course of performance-enhancing drugs, usually anabolic steroids, timed to a cutting diet phase so a lifter can get leaner while holding on to muscle.
card.note: Anabolic steroids are controlled substances in many countries with documented cardiovascular, hormonal and liver effects.

quick.overview:
A cutting cycle is the bodybuilding term for using anabolic steroids or related drugs during a cutting phase, the calorie-deficit stretch in which lifters shed body fat to reveal muscle. The stated aim is a leaner, more defined physique while limiting the muscle that normally gets lost when eating less.

Anabolic steroids increase protein synthesis and are described as favouring muscle over fat-storage cells. Controlled evidence for cut-specific protocols is sparse, and the drugs carry well-documented adverse effects.
quick.how: The cut itself combines eating below maintenance with training and cardio, often for a few months before a contest or a summer. In steroid-using circles, drugs are scheduled alongside that phase. This entry does not cover specific compounds, doses or schedules.
quick.risks: Steroid use is linked to unfavourable cholesterol changes, high blood pressure, heart enlargement, liver and kidney problems, suppression of natural testosterone, acne, hair loss and mood effects. Steroids are Schedule III in the US and Class C in the UK.

lead: A cutting cycle is a term in bodybuilding and gym culture for a period of anabolic steroid or related drug use aligned with a cutting phase [1][2]. The cutting phase is the stretch in which a lifter eats below maintenance calories, usually with cardio, to lose fat and reveal muscle definition [1].

The appeal for appearance is a leaner, harder physique while keeping muscle that a calorie deficit would otherwise cost. Wikipedia notes that most competitors cut for about 12-14 weeks before a contest, and that a larger deficit increases the risk of losing muscle [1]. Anabolic steroids are described as raising protein synthesis and possibly blunting muscle breakdown [2].
Use is not limited to competitors: a survey cited on Wikipedia found most users were non-competitive bodybuilders or non-athletes, often using for cosmetic reasons [2].

chain: Drugs used to help preserve muscle during the deficit
Lower body fat with muscle retained
angle.text: Lifters time drug use to the diet phase hoping to keep or add muscle while dieting down. The visible result sought is more definition at a lower body fat.

infobox: US Schedule III; UK Class C [2]

paras: The cutting phase follows an off-season in which the lifter eats a surplus to build muscle; cutting then removes the accumulated fat through a calorie deficit and cardio, with high protein emphasised [1]. Final contest prep may add carbohydrate loading and dehydration for sharper definition [1].

A cutting cycle layers drug use on top of this diet. Wikipedia notes that some bodybuilders use anabolic steroids and other performance-enhancing drugs to build muscle and recover faster, that most competitions prohibit them, and that some amateur federations do not test [1].

Anabolic steroids increase protein synthesis and muscle-cell formation and may reduce muscle breakdown [2]. A 2006 placebo-controlled trial of low-dose testosterone in elderly men with low testosterone found no benefit to body composition or physical performance [2]. Evidence specific to cutting protocols is not summarised in these references.

Documented effects of anabolic steroids include harmful cholesterol changes, hypertension, left ventricular hypertrophy, arrhythmia, heart attack, stroke and sudden death; liver damage with oral compounds; kidney problems; suppressed natural testosterone, testicular atrophy and reduced sperm production; gynecomastia; acne; hair loss; and mood changes including aggression [2]. Studies link bodybuilding to higher mortality, citing sudden cardiac death, drug use and extreme weight changes [1]. Steroids are a Schedule III controlled substance in the US and Class C in the UK, and a black market with counterfeit products exists [2].
No studies found on cutting cycles as a protocol.
